rubric.description: Critically reflect upon issues, concepts, theories and perspectives relevant to the subject, developing multiple arguments.

levels.name: Insufficient
levels.description: Descriptive, sometimes illogical or contradictory. Generalisations/statements made with scant evidence/references. Conclusions lack relevance validity.

levels.name: Satisfactory
levels.description: Some awareness of issues. Arguments emerging though not completely coherent. Some evidence/references to support views, but not always consistent. Some relevant conclusions.

levels.name: Good
levels.description: Issues identified within given areas. An emerging awareness of different stances and ability to use evidence/references to support a coherent argument. Broadly valid conclusions.

levels.name: Very Good
levels.description: Strong analytical ability. Acknowledgement of views of others. Arguments generally logical, coherently expressed, well organised and supported. Sound conclusions.

levels.name: Excellent
levels.description: Excellent analysis. Perceptive and persuasive points made within given area. Explicit acknowledgement of other stances. Arguments well-articulated, and logically developed with a range of evidence/references. Strong conclusions.

levels.name: Outstanding
levels.description: Logical, articulate analysis a consistent feature. Persuasive points made throughout the work within a highly articulate, balanced argument. Judiciously selected evidence/references, drawn from relevant research. Convincing conclusions.

rubric.description: Analyse and develop solutions to problems, using a range of problem solving tools and techniques.

levels.name: Insufficient
levels.description: Limited evidence of ability to apply methods appropriately to address a problem.

levels.name: Satisfactory
levels.description: Applies methods to address a problem, and some evidence of the complexity of the issues in the discipline.

levels.name: Good
levels.description: Applies methods accurately to address a well-defined problem, appreciating the complexity of the issues.

levels.name: Very Good
levels.description: Applies methods accurately to address a well-defined problem, examining the complexity of the issues.

levels.name: Excellent
levels.description: Applies methods accurately and very effectively to address a well-defined problem, appreciating the complexity of the issues.

levels.name: Outstanding
levels.description: Applies methods accurately and highly effectively to address a well-defined problem, appreciating the complexity of a range of issues.

rubric.description: Analyse political, social and environmental issues related to a range of professional contexts.

levels.name: Insufficient
levels.description: Descriptive generalised statements made with scant evidence/references.

levels.name: Satisfactory
levels.description: Some awareness of issues and some evidence/references to support views, but not always consistent.

levels.name: Good
levels.description: Issues identified within given areas. An emerging awareness of the complexities.

levels.name: Very Good
levels.description: Issues/challenges clearly identified within given areas. Awareness of the complexities examined and discussed with evidence/references.

levels.name: Excellent
levels.description: Excellent  analysis of  complex issues/challenges developed with a range of evidence/references.

levels.name: Outstanding
levels.description: Logical, articulate analysis of complex business issues/challenges with judiciously selected evidence/references.

rubric.description: Analyse and apply theories, skills and techniques to achieve practical outcomes in a range of real-world contexts/scenarios.

levels.name: Insufficient
levels.description: Limited evidence of ability to identify tools and methods appropriately and little evidence of application in the real world.

levels.name: Satisfactory
levels.description: Some method/tools/skills identified and used, applied to real world contexts.

levels.name: Good
levels.description: Appropriate method/tools/skills identified and applied in a real world context, with some appreciation the complexity of the issues.

levels.name: Very Good
levels.description: Method/tools identified and applied effectively in a real world context appreciating the complexity of the issues.

levels.name: Excellent
levels.description: Method/tools identified and applied very effectively in a real world context appreciating the complexity of the issues.

levels.name: Outstanding
levels.description: Method/tools identified and applied in a real world context highly effectively appreciating the complexity of a range of issues.

rubric.description: Analyse and apply digital tools to solve a range of problems and support effective communication.

levels.name: Insufficient
levels.description: Very limited evidence of ability to identify digital tools and methods and apply appropriately.

levels.name: Satisfactory
levels.description: Some digital method/tools identified and evidence of appropriate use in solving basic problems.

levels.name: Good
levels.description: Digital method/tools identified and applied, with some appreciation of the complexity of problems/communication.

levels.name: Very Good
levels.description: Digital method/tools identified and applied appreciating and examining the complexity of the problems/communication.

levels.name: Excellent
levels.description: Digital method/tools identified and applied very effectively appreciating the complexity of problems/communication.

levels.name: Outstanding
levels.description: Digital method/tools identified and applied accurately and highly effectively appreciating the complexity of a range problem/communication issues.

rubric.description: Apply professional and ethical working practices, acting in the best interest of the organisation.

levels.name: Insufficient
levels.description: Descriptive generalised statements made with scant evidence/references.

levels.name: Satisfactory
levels.description: Some understanding of professional practices/issues and some evidence/references to support views, but not always consistent.

levels.name: Good
levels.description: Understanding of professional practices/issues. An emerging awareness of ethical decision making.

levels.name: Very Good
levels.description: Understanding of professional practices/issues clearly identified within given areas. Awareness of the complexities of ethical decision making supported by evidence.

levels.name: Excellent
levels.description: Excellent understanding of professional practices/issues with an appreciation of the complexities of ethical decision making supported by a range of evidence.

levels.name: Outstanding
levels.description: Logical, articulate understanding of professional practices/issues with a strong appreciation of the complexities of ethical decision making supported by a range of evidence.

rubric.description: Apply collaboration processes to facilitate effective working relationships, share ideas and address challenges for mutual benefit.

levels.name: Insufficient
levels.description: Limited evidence of collaboration processes and skills identified for the assessment at this level.

levels.name: Satisfactory
levels.description: Some understanding of collaboration processes, with some evidence of working with others as a member of a group, or with stakeholders.

levels.name: Good
levels.description: Good understanding of collaboration processes, with evidence of working with others as a member of a group, or with stakeholders.

levels.name: Very Good
levels.description: Clear understanding of collaboration processes, with evidence of working with others as a member of a group, or with stakeholders supported with evidence.

levels.name: Excellent
levels.description: Excellent understanding of collaboration processes, with evidence of working with others as a member of a group, or with stakeholders supported with evidence.

levels.name: Outstanding
levels.description: Excellent understanding of collaboration processes, with judgement and evidence of the complexity of working with others as a member of a group, or with stakeholders.

rubric.description: Analyse and reflect on a range of ideas that inform evidence-based decision making.

levels.name: Insufficient
levels.description: Descriptive, sometimes illogical or contradictory. Generalisations/statements made with scant evidence. Conclusions lack relevance validity.

levels.name: Satisfactory
levels.description: Sense of argument emerging though not completely coherent. Some evidence to support views, but not always consistent. Some relevant conclusions.

levels.name: Good
levels.description: Issues investigated within given areas with an emerging awareness of different perspectives and ability to use evidence to support a coherent argument. Broadly valid conclusions.

levels.name: Very Good
levels.description: Strong analytical ability. Acknowledgement of views of others. Arguments generally logical, coherently expressed, well organised and supported. Sound conclusions.

levels.name: Excellent
levels.description: Excellent  analysis. Arguments well-articulated, with multiple perspectives identified and logically developed with a range of evidence. Strong conclusions

levels.name: Outstanding
levels.description: Logical, articulate analysis a consistent feature. Persuasive points made throughout the work within a highly articulate, balanced argument. Judiciously selected evidence.

rubric.description: Examine and apply a range of discipline-specific theories, concepts and skills, for practical business contexts.

levels.name: Insufficient
levels.description: Gaps in knowledge and superficial understanding of core knowledge and skills. Some inaccuracies.

levels.name: Satisfactory
levels.description: Broadly accurate knowledge and understanding of the  core knowledge and skills. Some elements missing and flaws evident.

levels.name: Good
levels.description: Sound, routine knowledge and understanding of the core knowledge and skills, main concepts and key theories. Some flaws may be evident.

levels.name: Very Good
levels.description: Consistent knowledge and understanding of the core knowledge and skills, examination of main concepts and key theories at this level.

levels.name: Excellent
levels.description: Detailed knowledge and understanding of the main concepts/ theories at this level. Awareness of multiple perspectives in of theory in the knowledge base.

levels.name: Outstanding
levels.description: Highly detailed knowledge and understanding of material, concepts and theories for this level of study. Awareness of the ambiguities and limitations of knowledge.

rubric.description: Communicate arguments and reasoning effectively, with a good understanding of audience and purpose within a range of business contexts.

levels.name: Insufficient
levels.description: Communication may have some merit but is inappropriately pitched for the audience.

levels.name: Satisfactory
levels.description: Communicates in a range of formats, including orally, appropriate to the discipline(s) audience and purpose, but with evident weaknesses.

levels.name: Good
levels.description: Communicates effectively in a range of formats, including orally, appropriate to the discipline(s), audience, and purpose.

levels.name: Very Good
levels.description: Communicates arguments well and consistently in a range of formats, including orally, appropriate to the discipline(s) audience and purpose.

levels.name: Excellent
levels.description: Communicates arguments and reasoning very effectively in a range of formats, including orally, appropriate to the discipline(s) audience and purpose.

levels.name: Outstanding
levels.description: Communicates arguments and reasoning highly effectively in a range of formats, including orally, appropriate to the discipline(s) audience and purpose.
